A. Certification of Qualified an Initiative Measure Establishing a Parcel Tax Collected by the City of Santa Monica for Funding for the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District and Adoption of Resolution to place Measure on the November 3, 2026 Ballot
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding that the resolution below is not a “project” subject to the California Environmental Quality Act;
2. Receive and file the attached Certification of Qualification regarding an Initiative Measure Establishing a Parcel Tax Collected by the City of Santa Monica for Funding for the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District by adding, Chapter 2.74 to the Santa Monica Municipal Code and establish an annual parcel tax of $495 per parcel of taxable real property located within the City of Santa Monica (“City”); and,
3. Adopt the attached resolution requesting and directing the actions necessary to place the measure on the November 3, 2026 , General Municipal Ballot.

B. Adoption of Resolutions Placing Proposed Ballot Measures Amending Articles XVIII, Rent Control Law, and XXIII, Housing Policies, of the City Charter on the November 3, 2026 Ballot
Recommended Actions
1. Adopt a finding of Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (common sense exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines; and
2. Per Rent Control Board recommendation and staff recommendation, adopt the attached resolution (Attachment A) placing a measure on the November 3, 2026, ballot that would amend Articles XVIII and XXIII of the City Charter to reaffirm the application of local just cause eviction laws, update term limit provisions for Rent Con trol Board Commissioners, update and clarify procedures for increasing the maximum annual rent controlled rental unit registration fee, clarify Rent Control Board authority to regulate time limits for deciding individual rent adjustment petitions, and add requirements for owners to evict tenants for non-compliance with affordable housing deed restrictions; and
3. Per Rent Control Board and staff recommendation, adopt the attached resolution (Attachment B) placing a measure on the November 3, 2026 ballot that would amend Articles XVIII and XXIII of the City Charter to prohibit evictions based on non-payment of rent when the tenant owes less than a fair threshold amount of rent; and
4. Per Rent Control Board and staff recommendation, adopt the attached resolution (Attachment C) placing a measure on the November 3, 2026 ballot that would amend Articles XVIII and XXIII of the City Charter to revise requirements for owners to evict tenants for breach of a rental agreement based on the addition of new occupants, re vise eviction protections for certain occupants remaining in a rental unit after the original tenant vacates, add just cause eviction protections to single-unit dwellings and condominiums, and modify requirements for good faith owner move in evictions from non-rent controlled rental units; and
5. Authorize City Councilmembers to file written arguments for or against and direct the City Attorney to prepare an impartial analysis for each measure.

COUNCIL TRAVEL  Mayor Torosis reported that she attended the U.S. Conference for Mayors
  National Endowment for the Arts Mayor’s Institute on City Design in
  Nashville, TN, where she gathered with six other mayors from across the
  country, and some design professionals to challenge intrinsic urban design
  challenges in our city, specifically the airport and what to do when it is
  converted. She also traveled to the Local Progress National Convening in
  Baltimore, Maryland. They addressed working on issues like how to handle
  data centers in our jurisdiction, and what responsible AI looks like. She also
  chatted with other jurisdictions who have set up their own local housing
  authorities, and social housing models for both affordable home ownership
  and affordable rental.

  Councilmember Negrete reported that she traveled to Coronado for
  Independent Cities Association, where she sits on their Executive Board as
  the Communications Director. She sat on two panels, one with Firefighters,
  consultants and Public Safety members where she shared what the city did
  with our system of care in terms of bringing ambulance services back in-
  house; she did a session on communication with constituents, difficult
  information, and transparency; and, she attended policy sessions around AI,
  the flock cameras, data sharing, data centers, and litigation and how it
  impacts cities.

  Councilmembers Raskin and Hall also attended the Local Progress National
  Convening Meeting, where there were more than 500 local and state elected
  officials across America. Councilmember Raskin shared he learned about
  models for a range of regulatory challenges and opportunities, tenant
  protections, municipal finance, and new revenue. Councilmember Hall
  shared how fortunate we are to live in California, specifically Santa Monica,
  where we have such strong tenant protection. Both the Mayor and
  Councilmember Hall attended the Local Progress National Convening
  meeting on a scholarship and there were no city funds used.

BALLOT MEASURES  Amending Articles XVIII, Rent Control Law, and XXIII, Housing
  Policies, of the City Charter on the November 3, 2026 Ballot, was

  Recommended Actions
  1. Adopt a finding of Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section
  15061(b)(3) (common sense exemption) of the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines; and
  2. Per Rent Control Board recommendation and staff recommendation,

  the November 3, 2026, ballot that would amend Articles XVIII and
  XXIII of the City Charter to reaffirm the application of local just
  cause eviction laws, update term limit provisions for Rent Control
  Board Commissioners, update and clarify procedures for increasing
  the maximum annual rent controlled rental unit registration fee,
  clarify Rent Control Board authority to regulate time limits for
  deciding individual rent adjustment petitions, and add requirements

   for owners to evict tenants for non-compliance with affordable
  housing deed restrictions; and
  3. Per Rent Control Board and staff recommendation, adopt the attached
  resolution (Attachment B) placing a measure on the November 3,
  2026 ballot that would amend Articles XVIII and XXIII of the City
  Charter to prohibit evictions based on non-payment of rent when the
  tenant owes less than a fair threshold amount of rent; and

  resolution (Attachment C) placing a measure on the November 3,
  2026 ballot that would amend Articles XVIII and XXIII of the City
